location.description: Nobleton is an unincorporated village in the Township of King, York Region, Ontario. Located south of the Oak Ridges Moraine — distinguishing it from King City (on the Moraine) and Schomberg (north of the Moraine). Positioned midway between King City and Bolton on the east-west route, and between Kleinburg and Schomberg on the north-south route. The Humber River meanders through the southwestern part of the community.
highway_access: Highway 400 (20 min east via King Road)
location.commute_to_toronto_drive: 30–45 min to downtown Toronto via Hwy 27/400
location.commute_to_pearson: less than 30 min to Toronto Pearson International Airport
location.go_train_note: No GO Train in Nobleton. Nearest GO station: King City GO (~10 min east) or Kleinburg GO Bus stop. Car-dependent commuter community.
location.source: Wikipedia Nobleton Ontario; comeexplorecanada.com/ontario/nobleton; Google Maps

history.founding: 1812 — Joseph Noble, a tavern keeper, settles at the northeast corner of Lot 5, Concession 9 (9th Concession and King Sideroad crossroads). He builds a homestead, general store, and tavern. The village grows around this crossroads and is named after him.
history.early_growth: Early settlers from England, Scotland, and the US. Taverns and hotels built to serve travellers. General stores and post office established. 1850s: board-and-batten blacksmith shop built in Nobleton — later moved to Black Creek Pioneer Village (where it still stands today).
history.religion: First congregation in 1840s. Wesleyan Methodist Church was Nobleton's first — closed 1896. Its materials were used to build the United Church, which still stands in Nobleton today.
history.arena: 1949 — Nobleton Arena built entirely by the community. One of the first community arenas in Ontario. Demolished 1977; replaced by the Nobleton Community Centre and Arena.
history.heritage_buildings: Hambly House — a majestic Victorian structure at the intersection of Hwy 27 and King Rd, one of Nobleton's most recognized heritage landmarks.
history.agricultural: King Township sustains over 41,000 acres of agricultural production across 239 farms — Nobleton sits within this working agricultural belt.
history.equestrian: Horse farms predominate on Nobleton's eastern periphery. Equestrian livestock breeding has been central to the area's character since the 19th century.
history.source: Wikipedia Nobleton Ontario; mosquitotoronto.com history of Nobleton; nobletonrealtors.ca

natural_environment.humber_river: Humber River meanders through the southwestern part of Nobleton. Designated Canadian Heritage River 1999.
natural_environment.king_creek: King Creek — a tributary of the East Humber — flows southerly from near Hwy 27 and 16th Side Road to meet the East Humber south of King Road, east of Nobleton.
natural_environment.moraine_position: South of Oak Ridges Moraine — rolling hills terrain without being on the Moraine ridge itself. Different natural character from King City (on-Moraine) and Schomberg (north of Moraine).
natural_environment.conservation: Conservation area covers the southwest of the community along the Humber River corridor.
natural_environment.source: Wikipedia Nobleton Ontario; Wikipedia Humber River Ontario
